newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan plans federal, provincial votes same day.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan plans federal, provincial votes same day.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker government said on Saturday it was planning to hold the next national and provincial elections on the same day -- February 3 -- contrary to the past practice of a few days' gap between the two votes.

Defence and Establishment Minister Shahid Hamid told reporters that "a decision in principle" had been taken to hold voting for the National Assembly (lower house) and for the four provincial assemblies on the same day to save money.
But a formal cabinet decision is yet to be taken.

President Farooq Leghari set February 3 for the National Assembly election when he dissolved the 217-seat house on November 5 and dismissed prime minister Benazir Bhutto's three-year-old government on charges of corruption and misrule.
But no date was set for the election of the provincial assemblies, which were also dissolved later by provincial governors on presidential instructions.
"It is in the interest of the nation and candidates that (two) elections should be held on the same day," Hamid said. "It will save huge money for the government and the candidates."
